games.name: Overtone
games.tagline: Not a game - a walk from one plucked string to the reason chords exist. Pluck it and meet the hidden ladder inside every note, pinch it in half to find the octave, then slide until the wobble goes calm: the fifth, the fourth, the third, discovered by ear. Stack your finds and they fuse into the major chord; slip one rung and hear it turn minor. Every claim demonstrated live, nothing to win.

games.name: Voicebox
games.tagline: Three fingers on a piano. A chord symbol appears - move your fingers to spell it, and the fewest semitones travelled is par. Hold the common tone, let the others lean, and the inversions every pianist actually plays turn out to be the cheap answer. Lock the last chord and your voicings play back as the song they were all along.

games.name: Bop
games.tagline: A loop that never stops and can't sound bad. Tap a beat into three glowing pads, thump a bassline that always lands on the right note, drag a finger up the ribbon and the melody snaps to the chord. You bring the rhythm and the shape; the machine plays it in tune, in time, in the pocket. No score, no levels - just noodle.

games.name: Afterlives
games.tagline: The same Tuesday morning, every time: tea, Dad's keys, and doors you can't afford yet. Live a life behind one of them - the shop, the storm, the beetles - die, and wake in the afterlife with whatever the soul kept: nerve, heart, stranger things. Traits only ever grow, and they open doors; some doors only ever say ???. Almost everything is locked. That's the game.

games.name: Threescore
games.tagline: A life in seven choices. One decision per decade, then a gravestone: sudden geese, drowned harvest fairs, small gods in canal pounds, blood banks with excellent skin. Eight worlds, 150 hand-carved endings; the graveyard fills as you live again, and the stones you earn buy the luck and heart to open doors fate kept shut. He gets seventy years, give or take. You get as many as you need.

games.name: Mini Levels
games.tagline: Sokoban that contains itself. One block on the board is a shrunken copy of the whole level - push it around, or step in through its door and you are back in the room you just left, one size down. Walk out through the outer wall instead and the level becomes a giant around you, with a second self already copying every move you make. Voids eat whatever you drop in them, boxes ride in and out of the nest with you, and every level has a par to beat.

games.name: Hydra
games.tagline: Cut it, get two. Pilot every snake at once with one relative command - pin one against a wall to desync the pack, cleave a snake into halves that crawl apart, push boxes, grow on pellets, and slide backward to fuse tails together again. Cover every diamond.

games.name: Terminus
games.tagline: Draw the track piece by scarce piece, then run every train at once. Lines may cross - trains may not. Fetch the key before the padlock, split colours apart, work each branch, and couple them back together in the right order.

games.name: Recurr
games.tagline: Design one tiny mark that is made of itself - tap cells to cycle self and other, hold to invert into ink or anti. Match the fractal in as few cells as par, reverse-engineer a random mark, or fuse two grids with a boolean operator.

games.name: Drip
games.tagline: Slide paint machines around the grid, then let the drops fall. Whatever lands first settles at the bottom; drops that land together share a band; dyes mix on the way down. Match the vial.

games.name: Cascade
games.tagline: Place stones - they never move. Win the majority of a block's 9 cells to take the block; a majority of blocks wins the game. Own ~31% of the board and still take it all.

games.name: Gridfire
games.tagline: Maze the grid with random tetromino blocks - every rotation sets both the wall and the aim. Chain elemental emitters into glowing conduits, funnel the horde through your kill zone, and hold twenty waves.

games.name: Lumen
games.tagline: Every stone is a lamp and a wall. Light along its row & column until blocked. Cells lit by only you are yours; lit by both, worthless. Most territory wins.

games.name: Lanternwake
games.tagline: You are the last Lamplighter. Sculpt the dark into a maze with lanterns and shutters - shades burn only where it is bright, and detour around the light you place. Then focus that light into weapons, draft your build, and hold eight waves and the Eclipse before the Long Night takes you.

games.name: Shipshape
games.tagline: Drag salvaged blocks onto your ship while rocks rain in - no build phase, just bullet time as a piece sockets into a gap. Every block is armour, a gun, and a puzzle: pack them tight to share welds, keep turrets exposed to fire, keep the core alive. Die, bank the salvage, evolve the tech tree, dive back in.

games.name: Fathom
games.tagline: Lower a powered cable of stations into an ocean trench. Read the 36h threat forecast, tune your defences, and push The Line deeper. When the deep wins, scuttle and surface - your old wreck is down there waiting to be salvaged.

games.name: Echo
games.tagline: Rewind on the pad to spawn a replay of your past self. Choreograph the yous you used to be - hold each other's doors, dodge your own history - then sequence a clean shutdown where every loop closes. Recursion, written in time.

games.name: Debt
games.tagline: Borrow anything from the future - use it now, then send one back through the portal to become the thing you borrowed. The exit only opens on a clean ledger. Bootstrap paradoxes, played as a pocket accounting game.

games.name: Fracture
games.tagline: Tap empty to place. Tap an enemy stone to shatter it into a new war. Win the line, own the cell.

games.name: Seed
games.tagline: Grow one little twig-shape by tapping buds. Every twig becomes that shape - again and again - into a tree that lights the suns, dodges the thorns, and fits the cave.

games.name: Loom
games.tagline: Author up to three rewrite rules. The loom runs them tick by tick, leftmost match first, until the bead thread matches the target - or unravels to nothing, or grows forever. Markov algorithms wearing a bead necklace.

games.name: Trine
games.tagline: Drag a mirror line anywhere - the shard flips across it, with a live ghost showing the landing. Stroke near a placed mirror to redraw just that one, and the whole chain of flips reshapes under your finger - grab one mirror of a turn and watch the shard orbit the crossing. Lines snap to neat angles; any pose is at most three flips away: that's a theorem, and the game makes you feel it. Sweep the stars, keep every flip clear of the voids, land home at par.

games.name: Kaleid
games.tagline: Plant a seed under the veil and the level's symmetry group blooms it into every copy at once - five turns, or five turns folded in mirrors. Reading the target's orbits IS the puzzle: a mark on an unseen fold line makes half as many copies, the still centre makes one, and par counts the families. Late scopes come unlabelled - read off 'five-fold, no mirror' like a crystallographer, then paint.

games.name: Mirror
games.tagline: Stroke a line across the grid and the light reflects across it - folding, doubling, and spilling off the edge until a few lit cells bloom into a symmetric pattern. Match the target constellation in the fewest mirrors: two mirrors make a turn, two parallel ones a slide. Chase par through sixteen levels, reverse-engineer a random mandala, or fold your own and share it.

games.name: Tile
games.tagline: One shape per level. Tap an empty cell to stamp it - its glowing eye lands where you touch; tap again to turn it through every way it fits there; hold to dissolve it. Fill the whole region with copies of that single polyomino, where hue is orientation so a finished tiling glows with its own hidden lattice. Fourteen levels from the deficient-board theorem to one-sided chirality, plus grown puzzles to share.

games.name: Allotmatic
games.tagline: A cosy pixel-art allotment where every act of automation is a geometric packing puzzle. Drag splashes from the well, tap ripe rows, send the pony cart to town - then research your way out of the chores with oddly-shaped sprinklers whose auras you must tile over the beds. Each new aura or crop shape makes the layout you were proud of an hour ago pleasantly obsolete. Make the whole plot tend itself, to a jaunty folk tune.

games.name: Ant War
games.tagline: Two ant colonies, one screen, and only one verb: build. Farms for income, hatcheries that breed attackers on their own, guard posts whose defenders intercept on the lane, sapper broods that chew through towers - then every eighteen seconds the war drum beats and both armies march whether you are ready or not. No unit micro, no manual sending: just the shape of your nest against the shape of theirs.

games.name: Ant War: Factions
games.tagline: The wild fork of Ant War, where the war drum itself is something you build. Horns make your beat slower and heavier, fifes make it faster and thinner, so each side marches to a tempo read off its own nest - and the enemy's countdown is on screen for you to play against. Mortars soften towers, charmers turn their ants into yours, predators hunt mid-lane. Still no powers, still no micro, just build.

games.name: Colony Clash
games.tagline: Tower defence in both directions along one shared pheromone trail. Every building is also a wall, so each placement re-routes the trail for their raiders and your ants alike - a long winding maze buys you more tower fire but costs you your own tempo. Farms pay more the nearer the midline you dare put them, raiders bite whatever they brush past, and late on you tear your own maze down to flood the gates open.
